answer: Interleaved heartbeat registration. Each new identity must submit its first N messages with inter-arrival gaps drawn from a wide distribution and a mandatory minimum spacing, so a falcon-fast burst of registrations is throttled at the ingress queue. The queue releases identities only as a gale of steady background traffic, and any identity whose early timing deviates is flagged as a relic and deprioritized. An attacker must rent real time: roughly one hour of wall-clock spacing per identity, serialized, capping registration throughput.
